variants.title: Young's modulus: steel wire, SWG 24
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: Steel is the stiffest of the three wires: the same load stretches it least.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of steel ~200 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 24 = 0.559 mm

variants.title: Young's modulus: steel wire, SWG 26
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: A thinner wire of the same material stretches more under the same load, because the stress is larger.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of steel ~200 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 26 = 0.457 mm

variants.title: Young's modulus: brass wire, SWG 22
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: Brass is about half as stiff as steel, so the same load gives about twice the extension.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of brass ~100 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 22 = 0.711 mm

variants.title: Young's modulus: brass wire, SWG 20
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: The thickest wire of the set: the extension is small, so read the micrometer with care.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of brass ~100 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 20 = 0.914 mm

variants.title: Young's modulus: copper wire, SWG 22
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: Copper is a little stiffer than brass and much softer than steel; keep the load small so it stays elastic.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of copper ~110 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 22 = 0.711 mm

variants.title: Young's modulus: copper wire, SWG 20
variants.method: Searle's apparatus, loads up to 2.5 kg
variants.note: The same copper drawn thicker: the extension falls as the square of the diameter.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of copper ~110 GPa); BS 3737 standard wire gauge: SWG 20 = 0.914 mm
